deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/03_Sol_Att_A_SOW_F.pdf ===== 1 SPECIFICATION - CLASS II VESSEL for PAPAHĀNAUMOKUĀKEA NATIONAL MARINE SANCTUARY 1] General Parameters (CLIN 0001) The Office of National Marine Sanctuaries requires one new and unused NOAA Class II research vessel for operations supporting Papahānaumokuākea National Marine Sanctuary. The vessel will be based in Oahu, HI, and will carry science and dive parties of up to nine people total. The vessel will conduct the following missions: Dive Training and Proficiency Emergency Response Acoustic Studies Whale Entanglement Response Vessel Inspections

deliverables_scope.text: BOOTS PURCHASE DESCRIPTION SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS: The Government has a requirement for the supply of varying quantities/sizes/types of safety boots for Fort Riley, Kansas. The primary salient characteristics must align with ASTM F2413-18 standards for protective footwear and emphasize complete waterproofing, slip resistance, and chemical/environmental hazard durability. SAFETY BOOTS-ANY BRAND or EQUAL No exclusions to Brands or colors as long as they meet the ASTM F2413-18 Standards MUCK BOOTS OR EQUAL-ANY BRAND No exclusions to Brands. Colors must be Black or Brown. Boots must meet the ASTM F2413-18 Standards SIZING, FIT, AND MEASUREMENT REQUIREMENTS 4.1 General Requirement The Contractor shall provide protective footwear (safety boots and muck boots) that accommodates the diverse physical demographics of the government workforce. All footwear must be manufactured using industry-standard lasts (molds) that ensure proper anatomical support, weight distribution, and compliance with ASTM F2413 safety clearances. 4.2 Required Size Matrix To ensure complete personnel outfitting, the Contractor shall offer the approved footwear in the following minimum size and width configurations: Men’s Sizing: Sizes 3.0 through 16.0. Women’s Sizing: Sizes 5.0 through 12.0 (If gender-specific lasts are not m

edure and pricing for ordering sizes outside of the standard matrix (e.g., Extra Wide EEEE, or sizes 17+) upon government request. 4.3 Technical Fit Standards Footwear provided by the Contractor must adhere to the following functional fit standards to prevent musculoskeletal injury and ensure operational readiness: Toe Clearance: Boots must provide a minimum of 0.5 inches (1/2") of clearance between the user's longest toe and the interior safety cap when standing. Heel Lock: The heel cup must securely anchor the foot. Vertical heel slip during a normal walking stride must not exceed 0.25 inches (1/4") to prevent friction injuries. Instep and Volume: The boot must allow the foot to rest flat on the footbed without lateral pinching at the metatarsal joints, while accommodating standard issued cold-weather or moisture-wicking socks. Calf Seal (Muck Boots Only): The upper shaft/collar of pull-on muck boots must feature a flexible binding that creates a flush seal against the mid-calf to prevent debris and fluid ingress, without restricting vascular circulation. Fit-Related Returns and Exchanges The Contractor shall guarantee the fit of all issued footwear. If a boot is issued to a government employee and deemed an improper fit under operational conditions (prior to heavy field soilage), th

Exchanges must be made within fifteen (15) business days of Contractor notification. 5.WARRANTY AND DEFECTIVE ITEMS 5.1 Standard Commercial Warranty The Contractor shall provide a standard commercial warranty for all supplied footwear. At a minimum, the warranty shall cover all items against defects in materials and workmanship for a period of not less than twelve (12) months from the date of final acceptance by the Government, or the duration of the manufacturer's standard commercial warranty, whichever is greater. 5.2 Covered Defects Under this warranty, a "defect" is defined as any failure of the footwear to meet the required performance specifications under normal operational use. Covered defects include, but are not limited to: Delamination: Separation of the outsole or midsole from the boot upper. Waterproofing Failure: Leakage or failure of the waterproof membrane (for safety boots) or the vulcanized rubber/neoprene shell (for muck boots) under normal water-exposure conditions. Structural Failure: Tearing of seams, unravelling of high-stress stitching, or premature breakdown of interior linings. Hardware Failure: Detachment or breakage of eyelets, speed hooks, zippers, or composite/steel safety toes shifting out of alignment. 5.3 Exclusions The warranty shall not cover damage resultin

oprene shell (for muck boots) under normal water-exposure conditions. Structural Failure: Tearing of seams, unravelling of high-stress stitching, or premature breakdown of interior linings. Hardware Failure: Detachment or breakage of eyelets, speed hooks, zippers, or composite/steel safety toes shifting out of alignment. 5.3 Exclusions The warranty shall not cover damage resulting from: Normal wear and tear (e.g., tread depletion from standard use). Intentional destruction, misuse, or abuse outside the scope of normal operational duties. Improper post-issue storage or exposure to unauthorized caustic chemicals not specified in the protective requirements. 5.4 Defect Reporting and Replacement Procedure In the event that the Government identifies defective footwear within the warranty period, the following procedures shall apply: Notification: The Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) or designated receiving official will notify the Contractor of the defect and request a Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA). Replacement Timeline: Upon notification, the Contractor shall provide a direct replacement of the defective item (in the exact same size and model) within fourteen (14) calendar days. Credit Option: If a direct replacement is unavailable, the Contractor shall issue a full credit or

Project Overview This project includes vegetation trimming, mulching, and clearing along 20,675 feet of designated trail and access routes within Marais des Cygnes National Wildlife Refuge. All work shall be performed in accordance with the treatment types delineated on the project map. 2. Location Marais des Cygnes National Wildlife Refuge Headquarters 24141 Kansas Hwy 52 Pleasanton, Kansas 66075 Office Phone: 913-352-8956 Office Hours 8am – 4:30pm 3. Scope of Work 3.1 Canopy Trimming (Orange and Y ellow Line Treatment Categories) • Trimming trees and woody vegetation from ground level up to a minimum height of 20 feet above the path of travel. • Mulching or grinding all branches, brush, and woody vegetation from the traveled path up to 25 feet from the center of the path, while protecting designated keep trees. • Keep trees will be identified and marked by refuge staff prior to work. • Protecting all good hardwood and designated keep trees; avoiding bark damage, root disturbance, and mechanical injury. • Ensuring all mulched vegetation or grindings do not exceed 3 inches in diameter and 18

dwood and designated keep trees; avoiding bark damage, root disturbance, and mechanical injury. • Ensuring all mulched vegetation or grindings do not exceed 3 inches in diameter and 18 inches in length. 3.2 Total Clearing (Red Line Treatment Category) • Removing and mulching all vegetation and all trees within the designated corridor. • Clearing width of 30 feet from the path of travel on each side. • Grinding stumps below grade or cutting them flush with the ground to eliminate tripping and catching hazards. • Ensuring mulch and grindings are no larger than 3 inches in diameter and 18 inches in length. 3.3 Ground Protection Requirements • Contractor must avoid rutting, soil displacement, puddling, and erosion, especially in wet or soft areas. • Work shall pause immediately when the refuge manager determines conditions are too wet for safe operation. 4.
